_comment: Provider entry commands for the framework dispatcher (dispatch.mjs). The framework owns scheduling; a provider is only a *callee* behind the task-interface ACL. Placeholders: {team} = the deployed team dir (~/.openclaw/team), {agent} = the dispatch agent argument. The task-panel entries below resolve to scripts that now SHIP WITH THIS REPOSITORY (team/scripts/**, deployed by install.sh into {team}/scripts/**) — no longer a 'base runtime must pre-deploy them' assumption; entry-path coupling is resolved. Provider dependency is now EXPLICIT (startup hard-fail, T-20261009-211234-providerdecouple): the entry scripts link the provider's ACL library at {team}/skills/task-ops/lib/ (installed by the task provider, intentionally not vendored) and, when it is absent, hard-fail with a clear 'provider 未安装' error + non-zero exit instead of a silent/cryptic no-op; dispatch.mjs still degrades to fire:false (never wakes a model) but its state.stderr carries that cause. checkAll now emits a {ok:true|false} envelope on its last line, so the dispatcher normalizes it (ok:false => fire:true, wakes only on failure) instead of classifying plain text as unparseable. The dispatcher bounds the entry with OPENCLAW_TEAM_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS (default 8000 ms) and the generated trigger passes exec({timeoutSeconds}); both stay under the Gateway's 30 s per-evaluation budget. Override per job with OPENCLAW_TEAM_POLL_CMD / OPENCLAW_TEAM_PATROL_CMD / OPENCLAW_TEAM_CHECKALL_CMD. Select a provider with OPENCLAW_TEAM_TASK_PROVIDER (default: task-panel).
